hook.line: Altamira is circling the block, and Tomás can't sleep. When someone else's move scares you, Spanish lets you say how much it scares you.
hook.es: Tengo miedo de que Altamira compre el edificio.
hook.en: I'm afraid Altamira will buy the building.

examples.es: Tengo miedo de que Altamira compre el edificio.
examples.en: I'm afraid Altamira will buy the building.

examples.es: Me preocupa que Vale no venga hoy.
examples.en: I'm worried Vale won't come today.

examples.es: Me da miedo que Simón se escape.
Me da pánico que me despidan.
Tengo miedo de que no vengas.

examples.es: Me preocupa que no tengas plata.
examples.en: I'm worried you don't have any money. (to a friend)

rule:
When you fear what someone else might do, use *que* and a verb with a changed ending: *compre*, *venga*, *vengas*. Not the future, not the usual present.

Three strengths:
*Me preocupa que...* (worried)
*Me da miedo que...* (scared)
*Me da pánico que...* (terrified)

*Tengo miedo de que...* is the same fear with *tener*.

When the fear is about your own action, drop *que* and use the infinitive: *Tengo miedo de perderlo.*
smallPrint: Teachers call this the subjunctive after verbs of emotion, and the infinitive when both clauses share the same subject.

readAndPick.es: Me preocupa que Vale no venga hoy.
options: I'm worried Vale won't come today.
I'm terrified Vale won't come today.

Tengo miedo de que lo pierdas.
Me da miedo hablar con él.
options: I'm scared to talk to him.
I'm scared you'll talk to him.

readAndPick.es: Me da miedo que hables con él.
options: I'm scared to talk to him.
I'm scared you'll talk to him.

Tengo miedo de que Altamira compre el edificio.

I'm afraid of buying the building.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *vengas* or *vienes*, then type the whole sentence: Tengo miedo de que no ___. (I'm afraid you won't come.)
yourTurn.answer: Tengo miedo de que no vengas.
yourTurn.why: After a fear about someone else, the verb takes the changed ending: *vengas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *me preocupa* or *me da pánico*, then type the whole sentence: ___ que Vale no venga hoy. (I'm worried Vale won't come today.)
yourTurn.answer: Me preocupa que Vale no venga hoy.
yourTurn.why: *Me preocupa* is the mild one: worried, not terrified.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I'm scared Simón will escape.
yourTurn.answer: Me da miedo que Simón se escape.
accept: Tengo miedo de que Simón se escape.
yourTurn.why: *Me da miedo que* plus the changed ending says what you're scared will happen.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I'm terrified they'll fire me.
yourTurn.answer: Me da pánico que me despidan.
yourTurn.why: *Pánico* is the strongest of the three.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I'm scared to talk to him. (I'm the one talking.)
yourTurn.answer: Me da miedo hablar con él.
accept: Tengo miedo de hablar con él.
yourTurn.why: Same person on both sides, so no *que*: just the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about *you* instead: *Tengo miedo de perderlo.* becomes: I'm afraid you'll lose him. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Tengo miedo de que lo pierdas.
yourTurn.why: A different person does the losing, so *que* comes back with the changed ending.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: It worries me that you don't have any money. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Me preocupa que no tengas plata.

pitfalls.why: Almost. English says *will come*, but after a fear Spanish uses the changed ending, not the future.

pitfalls.wrong: Tengo miedo de que perder a Vale.
pitfalls.right: Tengo miedo de perder a Vale.
pitfalls.why: Almost. When you are the one afraid and the one losing, use the infinitive and no *que*.

pitfalls.wrong: Yo me preocupo que no vengas.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Preocupa* works like *gusta*: the worry bothers you, so *me* comes first.

personal: Tell me one thing you fear someone else might do, or one thing that worries you about someone. Start with *Me preocupa que...* or *Tengo miedo de que...*.
